# Conflict Should Follow Escalation All interpersonal conflicts within a shift should follow a basic process of escalation. This means not jumping to violence immediately when something goes wrong, and especially not immediately resorting to lethal options.
Violence for the sake of self-defense does not fall under escalation, and you may respond to violence in turn, or with whatever is required to fend off your attacker. If you are a Security or Command member, you should [textlink="consider the consequences" link="ClauseSpL1"] of disproportionatel violence even for self-defense.
## Steps of Escalation The basic process of escalation is as follows. - 1. Words - 2. Threats of violence - 3. Subduing (such as non-lethals for security or flashes/sprays for command) - 4. Violence and physical altercation resulting in injuries - 5. Violence resulting in incapacitation - 6. Violence resulting in death
You should never be escalating to stage 6 if you started at stage 1. Think about the world from an IC perspective– you wouldn't kill a coworker for stealing your pen.
You should not overescalate for the situation, and minor disagreements should not result in life-threatening conflicts. Remember that your character should [textlink="value their life and continued employment." link="RPSpL1"]
## Validhunting [bold]Validhunting is not allowed[/bold]. This is the act of intentionally going after characters on the basis of them being an antagonist or aggressor. Keep in mind that [textlink="you should fear death" link="RPSpL1"], and that you have your own job to contend with.
Civilian personnel chasing military hostiles is validhunting. For example, the quartermaster should not be chasing an enemy operative into maintenance when the station has security personnel.
It is not validhunting to act in self-defense, or to respond to the death or injury of a significant other, theft of deeply sentimental property, or any other reasonable justification for putting your fear of death aside. However, your reason must be well-founded in characterization– do not invent reasons to chase after people who are likely to be hostile and armed.
## Hostiles And Enemies There may be attackers who strike the station and its personnel without chance of compromise, and unthinking/insane beings who cannot be reasoned with. You do not have to follow escalation expectations when dealing with NPCs, or with hostile forces that have already clearly communicated their intent.
However, you should still be mindful that this is a roleplaying game and not a PvP one, and avoid being the one to make the first move if you're on the defending side. Keep in mind that validhunting rules still apply, and just because you do not need to escalate does not mean you should freely attack player-controlled hostiles.
